text: Use a server-controlled tutoring sequence: material selection, diagnostic, editable skill map, one-question teaching turns, spaced review, and a mixed final assessment; the model supplies bounded explanations and questions while code decides the next state. Preserve the learner's ability to request a direct explanation, adjust difficulty, choose the next skill, or pause and resume.

Persist demonstrated skill levels 0-5 with cited attempt evidence, and show level/5 progress bars separately from session completion, recall due dates and engagement rewards. Require independent checks including later unaided recall for promotion, treat assisted answers as practice evidence, and show diagnostic levels as provisional until assessed.

Let school students upload their own selectable-text PDFs or paste notes, confirm an extracted outline and choose a chapter; asynchronously prepare source-linked skill cards, questions, answer rubrics and misconception hints, then serve short retrieval-grounded tutor turns. Start with text-dominant material and explicit unsupported-content handling for scans, handwritten work, diagrams, missing solutions and disputed claims; release additional formats only after extraction and grading checks.
